title: Strict Type Coercion Formatter
problemStatement: Implement `safeCast(value, targetType)` that explicitly and safely converts `value` to `'string'`, `'number'`, or `'boolean'`. For `'number'`, if conversion results in NaN, return `0` instead.
interviewTrap: Using `+value` or `parseInt` can cause subtle NaN or radix bugs. `Number(value)` with `Number.isNaN()` check is standard.

testCases.name: Safely converts string to number with NaN fallback
Casts valid numeric string to number
Casts empty string and non-empty string to boolean

details.name: Safely converts string to number with NaN fallback

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: The engine coerces primitives via internal algorithms. In loose equality (`==`), boolean values are first coerced to numbers, objects are coerced via `ToPrimitive(hint)`, and `null == undefined` is exclusively true.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Initialize execution context and environment records for Explicit Type Conversions & Truthiness.
2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.
